calc.title: Music Revenue Report 2026
calc.description: Interactive revenue forecast for an independent artist

calculation-logic.description: Since April 2024, tracks with <1000 streams over 12 months are not monetized. The final rate depends on listener geography and Premium subscription status.

tier_1.note: The US rate has risen to ~$0.0048 due to subscription price indexation.

tier_3.note: Minimum rates due to low cost of local subscriptions.

threshold_rule.title: 1000 Streams Threshold
threshold_rule.description: Official Spotify 2024 rule: tracks must reach a minimum of 1000 streams per year to start payouts.

payout_2025_report.title: Loud & Clear Report 2026
payout_2025_report.description: Spotify paid out $11 billion to rights holders in 2025. 70% of revenue goes to the industry.

ui-elements.notes: The sum of Tiers must equal 100% for correct calculation.

calculation-logic.description: Income consists of streaming payouts (where the Plus rate is 6.5x higher than the ad rate) and direct fan donations. The donation formula accounts for a ~10% service commission.

streaming.description: Payouts critically depend on whether the user has a Yandex Plus subscription.

donations.description: Direct support for artists. On average, 10,000 streams result in several donations.

yandex_rate_2026.title: Average Rate 2026
yandex_rate_2026.description: The average payout per 1000 streams is 50–65 ₽. The key driver is listening via the 'My Vibe' recommendation system.

donations_impact.title: Donations Tool
donations_impact.description: After the 'Unpacking 2025' update, donations are displayed in the artist's dashboard as a significant part of income.

calculation-logic.description: Total VK income consists of player streaming (where the VK Mix subscriber rate is 4.4x higher than the free rate) and payouts for track usage in VK Clips (UGC).

streaming.description: More than 60% of VK listenings come from the free version, which lowers the average rate.

video_ugc.description: Income for 1 million clip views with your track is approximately 4500 ₽.

vk_payout_2026.title: VK Rates 2026
vk_payout_2026.description: The average payout per 1000 streams in VK stays within the 18–25 ₽ range due to the specifics of the ad model in the CIS.

vk_clips_monetization.title: Clips Monetization
vk_clips_monetization.description: VK actively pays royalties for the use of audio in short videos by users.

calculation-logic.description: Apple pays per stream. The rate is higher if the track is available in Spatial Audio and if listeners are in Tier-1 countries (USA, Europe).

individual.note: The 'one cent' rate for individual plans in developed countries.

family.note: Reduced rate due to discount and family packages.

apple_penny_standard.title: One Cent Standard
apple_penny_standard.description: The average payout per stream on an individual plan is $0.01, which is significantly higher than competitors.

spatial_audio_boost.title: Spatial Audio Bonus
spatial_audio_boost.description: Since 2024, Apple applies a +10% royalty bonus for streams in Dolby Atmos format.

calculation-logic.description: YouTube income is the sum of streaming (YT Music), ads on long videos, Shorts fund payouts, and monetization of your track re-uploads by others (Content ID).

yt_main_video.name: Official Video
yt_main_video.description: Ad revenue from official music videos (Vevo/OAC).

yt_shorts.name: YouTube Shorts
yt_shorts.description: Payouts from the Shorts Creator Pool.

content_id.name: Content ID (UGC)
content_id.description: Income when others use your music in their videos.

yt_shorts_model.title: Shorts Payout Model 2026
yt_shorts_model.description: YouTube distributes 45% of Shorts ad revenue among creators and music rights holders.

yt_payout_stats.title: Lyor Cohen Report
yt_payout_stats.description: YouTube paid $9 billion to the industry in a year. The main growth comes from Content ID and Shorts.

calculation-logic.description: Income consists of standard royalties for user Reels (UGC), direct monetization of your own Reels (Ads share), and increased payouts from business accounts (BML).

reels_stories_ugc.name: Standard UGC (Reels & Stories)
reels_stories_ugc.description: Income from regular users using your track.

meta_ads_revenue.name: Official Reels Monetization
meta_ads_revenue.description: Direct monetization of content on the artist's profile (Bonus Program).

business_music_library.name: Business Music (BML)
business_music_library.description: Usage of music by brands. The rate is 5 times higher than standard.

meta_payout_leak.title: 2026 Payout Analytics
meta_payout_leak.description: According to reports, 1 million Reels views brings from $15 to $50 depending on account type and region.

business_library_impact.title: Business Music Layer
business_library_impact.description: Music in BML is available to 200 million business accounts, bringing artists increased royalties.

calculation-logic.description: Calculation is divided into regular videos (UGC) and commercial uses (CML). Brands pay on average 15-20 times more per creation, but their share in total volume is usually small.

ugc_creation_standard.name: Standard Creation (UGC)
ugc_creation_standard.description: Payout for the fact of track usage in a new video + for every 1000 views.

creator_rewards_program.name: TikTok Creator Rewards (Official)
creator_rewards_program.description: Direct payouts to the artist for qualified views of videos longer than 1 minute on their profile.

commercial_music_library.name: Commercial Music Library (CML)
commercial_music_library.description: Track usage by brands for advertising. Paid at a significantly higher rate.

tiktok_new_model_2024.title: New TikTok Payout Model
tiktok_new_model_2024.description: After 2024, TikTok considers not only the number of videos but also their reach (views).

creator_rewards_2026.title: Creator Rewards Program
creator_rewards_2026.description: The 2026 program pays about $0.50 per 1000 qualified views of long-form content.

calculation-logic.description: Payouts depend on the share of listeners with a SberPrime subscription. Artists who upload tracks in Hi-Fi quality receive a bonus of up to 15% for lossless format listenings.

streaming.description: Main income stream comes from users with an active SberPrime or SberPrime+ subscription.

hifi_bonus.description: Increased coefficient for listening in Hi-Fi quality (Lossless), which the service is actively pushing in 2026.

zvuk_market_share_2026.title: Market Share & Payouts
zvuk_market_share_2026.description: Zvuk maintains an average rate of 5-6 kopecks per stream from a subscriber, holding about 15% of the RU market.

hifi_promotion.title: Zvuk Hi-Fi Standard
hifi_promotion.description: Artists in high quality receive a distribution bonus from the royalty pool.

calculation-logic.description: Payouts are mainly formed from the MTS Premium subscription pool. The rate per subscriber stream is stable but lower than market leaders due to a high share of mobile operator bundle offers.

ecosystem_streaming.description: Main income stream — users with MTS Premium subscription.

mts_rate_2026.title: MTS Music Rates
mts_rate_2026.description: The average payout is 4.5–5.5 kopecks per stream. Indicators often correlate with Zvuk due to a shared backend.

mts_premium_reach.title: MTS Premium Ecosystem
mts_premium_reach.description: A base of 30 million users ensures a stable volume of royalties even for niche artists via algorithms.

calculation-logic.description: Deezer applies an Artist-Centric model: payouts are doubled (Boost) if an artist has more than 500 unique listeners. Streams via active search (Fan Engagement) also receive an additional increasing coefficient.

professional_boost.name: Professional Artist Boost
professional_boost.description: If you have passed the threshold, the value of each of your streams doubles.

active_search_boost.name: Fan Engagement Boost
active_search_boost.description: Streams from search bring up to 2 times more than just from playlists.

deezer_acps_launch.title: Artist-Centric Model
deezer_acps_launch.description: Deezer implemented the model to protect the income of real musicians from AI-noise dilution.

deezer_payout_rate_2026.title: Deezer Rates 2026
deezer_payout_rate_2026.description: The average payout varies from $0.004 to $0.008, making it one of the most profitable services.

calculation-logic.description: Bandcamp takes 15% from digital (drops to 10% at >$5k turnover) and 10% from merch. On 'Bandcamp Fridays', the platform commission is 0%. A 0.94 multiplier subtracts bank transaction fees.

revenue_share.threshold_description: When income > $5000/year, the digital goods commission drops to 10%.

special_events.friday_description: Days when the platform takes 0% commission.

bandcamp_fair_trade.title: Fair Trade
bandcamp_fair_trade.description: Artists receive an average of 82% from every sale after all deductions — the best indicator in the industry.

payment_processing_fees.title: Processing Fees
payment_processing_fees.description: Besides the platform share, an acquiring commission is held (usually 4-6% + fix).

calculation-logic.description: In addition to recording (master) royalties, authors receive mechanical royalties and performance rewards. Rates are regulated by government bodies (e.g., CRB in the USA).

mechanical.name: Mechanical Royalties
mechanical.description: Paid to the author for every digital stream. In 2026, the rate is about $0.0006.

performance.name: Public Performance
performance.description: The author's share within the streaming service for the fact of playback.

crb_rate_2026.title: CRB Phono IV Rates
crb_rate_2026.description: In 2026 in the USA, mechanical royalties reached 15.3% of total service revenue.

mlc_payouts_2026.title: MLC Reports
mlc_payouts_2026.description: The Mechanical Licensing Collective accelerated royalty distribution, increasing author income by 5-8%.

calculation-logic.description: Net profit = (Ticket revenue - 10% Operator commission - Rental, promo, and logistics costs) * Artist share (minus agent commission) + Merch sales profit (calculated at 20% listener-to-buyer conversion).

touring_economics_2026.title: Tour Economics 2026
touring_economics_2026.description: Due to rising logistics prices, the concert break-even point in 2026 occurs at 65% ticket sales.

merch_sales_stats.title: Merch as Salvation
merch_sales_stats.description: Merch sales at a concert add 15% to 30% to the net profit.

calculation-logic.description: With a POD model, you receive a fixed ~25%. With your own production, profit is higher, but production cost, acquiring commission (5%), and fixed logistics costs (5000 ₽) are subtracted.

merch_market_2026.title: CIS Merch Market
merch_market_2026.description: In 2026, merch accounts for up to 40% of independent artists' income. Most profitable items: hoodies and vinyl.

pod_vs_batch.title: Production Models
pod_vs_batch.description: Using POD services reduces margin to 20-30% but eliminates warehouse risks.

calculation-logic.description: Synchronization brings one-time large payouts. Usually, income is split between the author and the recording owner. If you are an independent artist, you receive everything minus the agent's commission (20%).

sync_rates_2026.title: Sync Rates 2026
sync_rates_2026.description: In 2026, the standard for an indie film is $500–$5,000, for a brand ad campaign — from $15,000.

sync_market_report_2026.title: Global Sync Market
sync_market_report_2026.description: Revenue grew by 20% thanks to demand from video games and original streaming series.

calculation-logic.description: Monthly income from fans. For Patreon, a ~13% commission is included. Income from Boosty (in rubles) is automatically converted to USD at a rate of 92 for correct summation.

creator_economy_report_2026.title: Creator Economy Report
creator_economy_report_2026.description: In 2026, income from 100 paid subscribers ($5) is equivalent to 150,000 monthly Spotify streams.

boosty_music_stats.title: Musicians on Boosty
boosty_music_stats.description: For CIS artists, Boosty has become the primary tool for subscription crowdfunding.

calculation-logic.description: Net income from crowdfunding minus platform commission (10-15%) and costs for producing/delivering rewards to fans. All calculations are in USD.

planeta_ru.name: Planeta.ru (RU)
planeta_ru.note: If 50-99% is raised, the commission is higher. If less than 50%, money is returned to fans.

crowdfunding_reality_2026.title: Crowdfunding Reality
crowdfunding_reality_2026.description: According to 2025-2026 statistics, about 35% of music project budgets goes to production and reward logistics.

calculation-logic.description: Monthly income. Consists of direct sales on audio stocks (minus 30% platform commission) and payouts for background broadcast in business locations (retail, cafes, gyms).

audio_stocks.name: Audio Stocks (Pond5, AudioJungle)
audio_stocks.description: Direct license sales for video, podcasts, and local advertising.

b2b_background.name: Background Music (Retail, Gyms)
b2b_background.description: Payouts from Muzlab, Soundtrack Your Brand, etc., for playing tracks in networks.

stock_licensing_trends.title: Micro-licensing Trends 2026
stock_licensing_trends.description: The social media license market has become more accessible through subscription models where artists get a fixed share of the platform pool.

calculation-logic.description: In China, the stream rate is extremely low, but there is huge income from virtual gifts and karaoke features (up to 50% of artist income).
Average rates for emerging markets. Anghami (Middle East) pays above the regional average.
The rate is stable and comparable to Spotify. Main traffic comes via Alexa devices.
Services with the highest payouts in the industry due to the lack of a free tier and focus on Hi-Res.
SoundCloud uses the Fan-Powered Royalties model. If your fans listen to you a lot and often, the rate grows (Fan Loyalty). Next Pro subscription is required to receive full payouts directly.

slides.title: The Music Industry Is Changing
slides.description: AI is reducing the value of music itself as a product. The primary asset is becoming the community around the artist.
slides.help: Start with the market challenge. Music is becoming abundant and inexpensive. Generative AI is dramatically increasing the amount of content available. Artists who know how to build meaningful relationships with their audience will be the winners.
items: Attention becomes the most valuable resource
Fan communities become a new asset

slides.title: The Problem with Modern Streaming Platforms
slides.description: Streaming platforms provide plays, but they do not create relationships between artists and listeners.
slides.help: Lead into the idea that Spotify, Yandex Music, and VK Music work well as catalogs but perform poorly as social platforms.
items: Artists do not know their audience

slides.title: Bilbo Is Not a Streaming Platform
slides.description: Bilbo is a music ecosystem built inside messaging platforms.
slides.help: It is important to communicate that we are not building another music player. We are building a communication layer. We are not competing for the streaming market; we are creating a market for social interaction around music.
items: A social layer built around music
Direct tools for the Creator Economy

slides.title: Where People Already Communicate
slides.description: Bilbo operates within existing communication environments rather than trying to attract users away from them.
slides.help: Emphasize Telegram and MAX as natural environments for interaction.

slides.title: A New Economy for Artists
slides.description: Bilbo helps artists earn directly from their relationships with their audience.
slides.help: A very important slide. Highlight the difference from traditional streaming services.

slides.title: Direct Artist ↔ Fan Connection
slides.description: Every interaction can be transformed into value for both sides.
examples: Release → delivered directly to the artist's audience
Community → participation in the artist's growth

slides.title: Transparent Analytics
slides.description: Artists see not only streams but also their entire community.
slides.help: A very strong argument for artists and labels.

slides.title: A New Subscription Model
slides.description: Only the artists a user actually listens to receive the user's money.
slides.help: This is potentially one of the strongest slides.
notes: 1% can be allocated to the playlist owner

slides.title: Strategic Value
slides.description: A platform for building a proprietary music vertical within a brand ecosystem.
slides.help: Show how the product addresses the needs of a major player in audience retention and loyalty building without directly competing with media giants.

slides.title: Synergy, Not Competition
slides.description: Bilbo effectively complements traditional streaming infrastructure.
slides.help: A slide designed to address concerns about market saturation. We explain that existing giants are storefronts, while we provide a space for interaction.

slides.title: Scalability and Extensibility
slides.description: Bilbo adapts to different audiences, markets, and usage scenarios.
slides.help: Demonstrate that the ecosystem is not limited to its current functionality.

slides.title: The Bilbo Ecosystem
slides.description: An entry point into the future development of the music world.
slides.help: Do not explain every component in detail. Use it as a map of directions for discussion.
